=== TOOLING NOTES ===
(1) NEW, AND IT SILENTLY BREAKS SCAN E. `gh` on this machine emits verbose trace lines to STDOUT ('* Request at 2026-08-03 00:51:58 ... * Request to https://api.github.com/... * Request took 249ms') interleaved with the JSON payload. board-scan.md's Scan E pipes `gh run list --json ...` straight into jq, so the parse fails and EVERY gate classifies as `unknown`. The classification table's promise that unknown 'NEVER collapses to ok' held and did its job -- but three false `unknown`s would have hidden a real six-night ALARM. Fix is one filter: `gh run list ... | grep -v '^\*'`. Recommend adding it to Scan E in board-scan.md; the same hazard applies to every other `gh --json | jq` in the skill tree. Root cause not chased (likely GH_DEBUG or similar in the scheduler env), but the filter is correct regardless.
(2) dcg blocks MORE of Scan D/E than the existing note admits. The documented literal-path form (`D="/tmp/ac_board_scan_scratch"; ... > "$D/ranges"`) is STILL blocked by core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-dynamic-path, because $D is shell-expanded. Only a fully literal `> /tmp/ac_board_scan_scratch/ranges` runs. board-scan.md's wording ('A LITERAL scratch path, not $(mktemp -d)') reads as if assigning a literal to a variable is enough -- it is not. Scan E additionally would not run at all in the documented shape; it had to be rewritten without temp files. Worth correcting the note to show the fully-literal redirect target.
(3) jq precedence trap, cost two failed queries: `.dependencies//[] | .[]` does NOT parse as expected -- write `(.dependencies//[])[]`. Separately, inside `select($epics|index(.issue_id))` the `.` rebinds to $epics, silently producing 'Cannot index array with string'; bind first (`(.issue_id) as $a | select($epics|index($a))`). Both are generic jq hazards that will bite any future edge-table query.
(4) `br sync --flush-only` again reported 'Nothing to export (no dirty issues)' after a label removal and a `br create`, and again both had already landed in issues.jsonl. Confirms last night's read: br 0.2.16 flushes eagerly. Verifying against the JSONL rather than the command's output is the correct standing practice.
